chapter_title: Concerning the Four Fathers; what they are like.

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
As in a person there are inner powers that cannot be directly seized or harmed, and outer functions that can be handled and therefore struck, so in the whole ordered Divine reality there is what remains withdrawn in interior holiness and what stands forth in outward operation. Some Divine things abide beyond assault, and some enter the level where conflict and injury can be felt.

In the same way, the ruling life within a person is held in the deep interiors of the mind and is not exposed to the senses; so the Divine of truth abides concealed in His own interior kingdom and is not put on display before the desolate outer state.

Yet there is also a constant power of discernment that stands openly present and gives illumination, and therefore a paired, steady disclosure of wisdom shines throughout all lower orders and all effects. Wisdom in its enlightening office is not withdrawn, just as discernment in its outward act is not hidden.

But the living human spirit, while it rests in a state that seems quiet and unresisting, is nevertheless seized at the outward level and struck by a sufficient set of bodily cravings and natural compulsions that batter it and work to ruin it. In that outer degree it can be constrained and dominated, and so it suffers injury.

There is also an outward faculty of utterance and doctrine that announces, corrects, and makes known everything occurring in a person, inwardly and outwardly, including the mind’s reflections and the body’s learned impressions. This outward expression makes conditions manifest, declaring what is noble and what is disgraceful in the life, and uncovering the distress of a life made sick by its evils.

So too the Divine revealer who proceeds from the highest Divine good makes all things known: outer and inner, higher and lower. He discloses even the interior heavens that are not exposed to outward sight, and he discloses the openly shining forms of wisdom that are perceived. He lays open their glory and the Divine good that dwells within them.

And concerning the injuries and assaults suffered by the living spirit, he is the one who brings them to light. He also teaches about its rest, and he discloses the way its stains are removed and its soundness restored.

paragraph_translations.translation: In a person there are inner powers that cannot be directly seized, and there are outer functions that stand exposed to contact. The exposed functions can be handled and therefore struck and injured, while the inner ones cannot be laid hold of in the same way and so do not receive such assaults.

So it is with the whole ordered Divine reality that we reflect in our measure: some things remain withdrawn in interior holiness, and some are outwardly present in operation. Some abide far from assault and suffering, while some enter the level where blows and wounds can be felt.
paragraph_translations.notes: “This entire greatness” is taken as the whole Divine-spiritual order; the exact scope is slightly ambiguous.

paragraph_translations.translation: Likewise, the ruling life within a person is hidden in the deep interiors of the mind and is not displayed to outward notice. In the same way the Divine of truth abides concealed in His own interior kingdom, not set forth before the desolate outer state.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Outer desolation” resists clean rendering; taken as an external state devoid of living good and truth.

paragraph_translations.translation: And as there is a paired power of discernment that stands visibly present and provides illumination for life, so there is a constant dual disclosure of wisdom that shines and is acknowledged throughout all lower orders and all effects. This enlightening wisdom is not withdrawn.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Two light ships” is forced into a dual, publicly shining mode of wisdom/discernment; the specific “two” could also mean will/understanding acting together.

paragraph_translations.translation: The living human spirit is also of this kind: it is held in a state that seems like silence and stillness, yet in that outwardly accessible condition it is seized and struck by a sufficient set of bodily cravings and natural compulsions that batter it and work to ruin it. In that degree it can be constrained and dominated, and so it suffers injury.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Five fleshes” is taken as a sufficient set of bodily lusts/compulsions; exact taxonomy is unclear.

paragraph_translations.translation: There is also an outward faculty of utterance and doctrine that announces, reproves, and makes known everything that takes place in a person, inwardly and outwardly, including the mind’s deliberations and the body’s acquired impressions. This outward expression renders things manifest, declaring what is honorable and what is shameful, and uncovering the distress of a life made sick by its evils.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Tongue” is rendered as outward expression/teaching; “sores” as active evils producing pain.

paragraph_translations.translation: This is the character of the Divine revealer who proceeds from the highest Divine good: he makes all things manifest, inner and outer, higher and lower. Whether it concerns interior heavens that remain hidden from outward sight, or the openly shining forms of wisdom that are perceived, he is the one who discloses them. He also reveals their glory and the Divine good dwelling within them.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Jesus the Splendour” is translated by function as revealer proceeding from the Divine; “aeons” read as interior heavens/orders.

paragraph_translations.translation: And regarding the assaults and injuries suffered by the living spirit, he is the one who brings them to light. He also teaches about its rest, and he discloses how it is purified and restored to soundness.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single teaching: it lays out a threefold distinction—hidden interiors, visible illuminations, and outwardly exposed levels that can be harmed—then identifies a revelatory Divine function that makes both glory and injury known and leads toward purification and healing. The only strain is the specificity of the paired lights and the set of five bodily agents, which are clear in structure but not fully determinate in detail.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential opening: the hidden/visible distinction is taught by what body-parts *undergo* (can be grasped, struck, wounded) versus what they do not undergo. No narrative seam or foreign list-material.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by function/condition: “limbs that are hidden… others… visible… can be grasped and receive blows and wounds, whilst others can neither be grasped nor receive blows” (¶1). ¶2 cleanly transfers the same experiential logic to “this entire greatness… some… hidden… some… visible… far away from the blows… whilst some… receives blows and wounds.” The spiritual reading’s notes only register mild scope ambiguity (“entire greatness”) but no stumble or forced patching.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential identification of the First Father as ‘directive of the body that lives within’: the Father corresponds by *hidden interior governance* (life-directive in storehouses) rather than by territorial administration. No intrusion of ranked powers or jurisdiction language.
findings.evidence: “the directive of the body that lives within, hidden in the storehouses inside the body and unseen. So it is also how the Father… exists; as he too is hidden in his kingdom” (¶3). The spiritual reading matches this naturally (“ruling life… hidden… so the Divine of truth… concealed”), indicating the sense arises directly from bodily function (inner directive).

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty (not a likely insertion): a correspondential analogy is present, but the mapping to Manichaean cosmological technicals (“two light ships”) produces interpretive strain. The paragraph still teaches by function (illumination/visibility), not by administration; the ‘two’ is not developed as a roster or hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The teaching is functional: “two eyes… visible… the body's source of illumination; so there are also these two light ships that shine and are seen… The light has never been hidden” (¶4). The spiritual reading explicitly reports strain: “Two light ships is forced into a dual… mode of wisdom/discernment; the specific ‘two’ could also mean…” That is a semantic/identificatory difficulty (what exactly are the ‘two ships’ in this chapter’s analogy), but removing it would collapse the chapter’s intended second correspondence (visible illuminators).

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty within a coherent correspondential move: the paragraph shifts from ‘visible/hidden organs’ to the soul’s vulnerability and introduces a fixed Manichaean-sounding numeral phrase (“five fleshes”). The reading stumbles on taxonomy, but the sentence still functions as ‘what can be grasped gets wounded’—not an administrative inventory.
findings.evidence: Correspondential core: “living soul… in apparent silence… is grasped and receives blows… destroy… strike it… can be grasped and mastered, can receive blows and wounds” (¶5), which continues ¶1’s ‘graspable → woundable’ logic. The stumble is the embedded technical label: “these five fleshes,” which the spiritual reading notes as unclear and non-determinate (“exact taxonomy is unclear”). This is ‘mixed’ only in the sense of a technical numeral tag inside an otherwise functional correspondence; it is not jurisdictional governance language.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential development: ‘tongue’ is presented as an outward faculty whose *function* is disclosure/reproof, matching the chapter’s theme of visible/outward mediation. No named authorities, no territorial ranks.
findings.evidence: “this tongue that speaks, proclaims, reprimands and reveals… inside and outside… makes it manifest… proclaims… honour and shame… speaks, unveiling the pain…” (¶6). The spiritual reading tracks smoothly (“outward faculty of utterance and doctrine”), with no note of mismatch.

findings.diagnosis: Expansion at a seam: a christological identification overlays the prior functional correspondence (‘tongue’ as revealer) by inserting a named salvific agent (“Jesus the Splendour… sent from the greatness”). The narrative still flows, but the voice shifts from analogy to doctrinal identification, matching a typical Mani seam-addition (naming an eternal function with a historical/sectarian figure + ‘sent’ formula).
findings.evidence: Seam-marker and identification: “This is also what Jesus the Splendour is like, who shall be sent from the greatness” (¶7). This recasts the just-given functional faculty (“tongue… reveals”) into a doctrinal personage and mission clause (“sent”). The spiritual reading flags this by having to translate by function rather than by the text’s explicit naming (“Jesus the Splendour is translated by function as revealer”), i.e., it has to *neutralize* the proper name to keep the correspondential thread. ¶7-8 also add systematizing scope (“outer and inner… above and below… aeons… ships of light”) and soteriological addendum (“cleansing and healing,” ¶8), which reads like an appended interpretive application of the earlier analogy rather than the analogy itself.
findings.scope:
Remove ¶7-8 in full:

“¶7: This is also what Jesus the Splendour is like, who shall be sent from the greatness. He manifests and reveals about everything, both the external and the internal, both what is above and what is below. Be it about the outer aeons that are hidden and not displayed, or about the ships of light that are seen: he is the one who unveils about them. He is also the one who reveals about their glory, and the greatness that dwells in them.

¶8: And regarding this beating and wounding of the living soul, Jesus is the one who reveals it. He also preaches about (the soul) and its peace. He reveals about its cleansing and healing.”

textual_criticism.summary: 6 findings: 4 clean correspondential substrate blocks (¶1-3, ¶6) confirmed; 2 genuine/semantic difficulties without excision (¶4 ‘two light ships’, ¶5 ‘five fleshes’); 1 seam-expansion identified (¶7-8) where christological naming and ‘sent’ formula overlay the functional ‘tongue/revealer’ correspondence. Recommendations: excise 1 block (¶7-8), none for the rest; no pure administrative overlay blocks in this chapter.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Just as the corporeal body has limbs that are hidden, so it also has others that are visible. They can be seen upon it, they can be grasped and receive blows and wounds, whilst others can neither be grasped nor receive blows.

So it is also with this entire greatness, as we resemble it. Some of it is hidden, whilst some of it is visible; some of it is far away from the blows and suffering, whilst some of it receives blows and wounds.

Now, thus the directive of the body that lives within, hidden in the storehouses inside the body and unseen. So it is also how the Father, the God of truth, exists; as he too is hidden in his kingdom, not displayed before this outer desolation.

Thus, too, the body has two eyes that are visible and seen, and are even the body's source of illumination; so there are also these two light ships that shine and are seen in the entire universe and the whole of creation. The light has never been hidden, just like the two eyes of the body.

The living soul too is like this; it is established in apparent silence. In its apparent silence it is grasped and receives blows from these five fleshes, which destroy (the soul) and strike it. It can be likened to the mystery of the corporeal body, as it can be grasped and mastered, can receive blows and wounds.

⟨p.152⟩ Also, thus this tongue that speaks, proclaims, reprimands and reveals about everything happening in this body, inside and outside, also the considerations and bodily knowledges. The tongue, which is outside, makes it manifest. It also proclaims about the honour and shame of the body. And it speaks, unveiling the pain of the body that is sick from its sores.

changes_summary: Applied Finding 6 (Recommendation: excise): removed ¶7–8 in full as a seam-expansion with christological naming and ‘sent’ formula overlaying the functional correspondence. No other paragraphs were modified (Findings 1–5: none/annotate only).
